facts.statement: Centrornis majori was an extinct species of large goose belonging to the shelduck subfamily.
facts.quote: The Malagasy sheldgoose (Centrornis majori) is an extinct monotypic species of large goose in the shelduck subfamily.

facts.statement: The species was described from subfossil remains found in central Madagascar that were radiocarbon dated to approximately 17,000 years ago.
facts.quote: It was described from subfossil remains radiocarbon dated to about 17,000 years ago, found in central Madagascar.

facts.statement: The genus Centrornis was established by Andrews in 1897.
Centrornis is classified within the family Anatidae.
Centrornis lived from the Late Pleistocene through the Holocene, spanning from 0.129 to 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Centrornis in the Paleobiology Database.
